Parent: Officer Buckle knew more safety tips than anyone else in Napville. Every time he thought of a new one, he thumb-tacked it to his bulletin board.
Child: (looks at the tablet, listening attentively)
Parent: Safety tip number seventy-seven: never stand on a swivel chair.
Child: (pointing at the tablet)
Parent: Hey.
Child: (looking up at the parent and then back at the tablet)
Parent: Oops, sorry. You can do the next page.
Child: (starts to interact with the tablet, ready to turn the page)
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Officer Buckle shared his safety tips with the students at Napville School. Nobody ever listened. Sometimes there was snoring."
Child: (looking at the tablet and pointing)

Parent: "Afterward it was business as usual. Mrs. Topple, the principal, took down the welcome banner. "Never stand on a swivel," said Officer Buckle. But Mr. Topple... But Mrs. Topple didn't hear him."
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "One day, Napville's police department brought a dog, a police dog named Gloria. When it was time for Officer Buckle to give the safety speech at the school, Gloria went along."
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "And do it."
Child: (looking at the tablet and pointing)
Parent: ""Children, this is Gloria," announced Officer Buckle. "Gloria obeys my commands. Gloria, sit!" And Gloria sat."
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Officer Buckle gave safety tip number one: keep your shoe laces tied. The children sat up and stared. Officer Buckle checked to see if Gloria was sitting at attention. She was."
Child: (looking at the tablet and pointing)

Parent: ""Safety tip number two," said Officer Buckle, "always swipe up spills before someone slips and falls." The children's eyes popped. Officer Buckle checked on Gloria again. "Good dog!" He said. Officer Buckle thought of a safety tip he had discovered that morning."
Child: (looking at the tablet with another child approaching)
Parent: ""Never leave a thumb-tack where you might sit on it." The audience roared."
Child: (looking at the tablet, hand on chin)

Parent: "Officer Buckley grinned. He said the rest of the tips with plenty of expression. The children clapped their hands and cheered. Some of them laughed until they cried. Officer Buckle was surprised. He had never noticed how many funny safety tips could be."
Child: (still looking at the tablet, hand on chin, leaning in closer)

Parent: "After this safety speech, there wasn't a single accident. The next day, an enormous envelope arrived at the police station. It was stuffed with thank you letters from students at Napville School."
Child: (looking at the tablet, smiling, and leaning closer to the parent)
Parent: "Look, some of them say: 'Dear Gloria and Officer Buckle, thanks for coming to our school. You were nice. Your friend, George.'"
Child: (excitedly pointing at the tablet)
Parent: "Every letter had a drawing of Gloria on it. Officer Buckle thought that the drawings showed a lot of imagination."
Child: (still pointing at the tablet, smiling)
Parent: " 'Dear Gloria and Officer Buckle,' that's the same one."
Child: (enthusiastically pointing at a specific spot on the tablet)
Parent: "His favorite letter was written on a star-shaped piece of paper. It said, 'You and Gloria make a good team. Your friend Claire. P.S. I always wear a crash helmet.'"
Child: (still pointing at the tablet, looking up at the parent, excited)
Parent: "Safety tip number seven. 'You and Gloria make a good team. Your friend Claire.'"
Child: (looking at the tablet while the parent is reading the story)
Parent: "Officer Buckle was thumb-tacking Claire's letter to his bulletin board when the phone started ringing. Grade schools, high-schools, and daycare centers were calling about the safety speech."
Child: (still looking at the tablet, engaged with the story)
Child: (leans head on hand while looking at the tablet)
Parent: ""Officer Buckle," they said, "our students want to hear your safety tips. And please bring along that police dog." Officer Buckle told his safety tips to...Oh, you skipped a page."
Child: (briefly looks at the parent, then looks back at the tablet)
Child: (leaning head on hand, continuing to look at the tablet)
Parent: "Officer Buckle told his safety tips to three-hundred and thirteen schools. Everywhere he and Gloria went, children sat up and listened."
Child: (maintaining focus on the tablet, hand still supporting head)
Child: (head still leaning on hand, looks closely at the tablet)
Parent: "Now you can turn the page."
Child: (reaches to turn the page on the tablet)
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the book)
Parent: "After every speech, Officer Buckle took Gloria out for ice-cream. Officer Buckle loved having a buddy."
Child: (leaning over and resting chin on hand, looking at book)
Child: (leaning to the side, looking away from the book)
Parent: "Want to turn the page or want me to?"
Child: (leaning back up, looking at the parent)
Child: (pointing at the book, looking engaged)
Parent: "Then one day a television news team videotaped Officer Buckle in the state college auditorium."
Child: (nodding and smiling)
Child: (holding up a different book, showing it to the parent)
Parent: "We're looking at the story, Felix."
Child: (lowering the book and looking back at the tablet)
Parent: (turning the page on the tablet) "When he finished safety tip number ninety-nine, 'do not go swimming during electrical storms,' the students jumped to their feet and applauded."
Child: (holding a book, looking at the tablet)
Parent: (smiling, looking at the tablet) "Bravo! Bravo!" They cheered. Officer Buckle bowed again and again."
Child: (still holding the book, looking at the tablet)
Parent: (pointing at the tablet) "Now that guy is in that corner."
Child: "What?"

Parent: (looking at the child, then back at the tablet) "That night Officer Buckle watched himself on the ten o'clock news. The next day, the principal of Napville school called on the police station. 'Good morning! Officer Buckle, it's time for our safety speech.' Officer Buckle frowned. 'I'm not giving any more speeches. Nobody listens to me anyway.' 'Oh.' Said Mrs. Topple. 'Well, how about Gloria, could she come?'"
Child: (looking at the tablet, smiling)

Parent: (turning the page) "Someone else from the police station gave Gloria a ride to school. Gloria sat on stage looking lonely, then she fell asleep. So did the audience. After Gloria left, Napville School had its biggest accident ever."
Child: (thinking, with finger on their chin)
Child: (sitting next to the parent, both looking at the tablet)

Child: (looks back at the tablet, more engaged again)

Parent: "Camilla Train loves lima beans, but she never ate them. All of her friends hated lima beans and she wanted to fit in. Camilla was always worried about what other people thought of her. Today she was fretting even more than usual. It was the first day of school and she couldn't decide what to wear."
Child: (nods slightly, still watching the tablet)
Parent: (continues to read from the tablet)
Child: (sitting with hands on cheeks, looking at the tablet)
Parent: "There were so many people to impress. She tried on forty-two outfits, but none seemed quite right. She put on a pretty red dress and looked in the mirror, then she screamed."
Child: (excitedly reacting, hands up)
Parent: Not seen reacting.
Child: (smiling widely, looking at parent)
Parent: "Ahhhhhh."
Child: (leaning forward, looking at tablet with parent)
Parent: "Her mother ran into the room, and she screamed too. 'Oh my heavens!' she cried."

Parent: "Just ignore [inaudible 00:07:24]."
Child: (same position, attentive)

Parent: "'You're completely covered with stripes.' This was certainly true. Camilla was striped from head to toe. She looked like a rainbow. Miss Cream felt Camilla's forehead, 'Do you feel all right?' she asked. 'I feel fine,' Camilla answered, 'but just look at me.'"
Child: (leaning against parent, slightly turned away from screen)

Parent: "'You get back in this bed this instant,' her mother ordered. 'You're not going to school today.' Camilla was relieved. She didn't want to miss the first day of school, but she was afraid of what the other kids would say."

Parent: And she had no idea what to wear with those crazy stripes. That afternoon, Doctor Bumble came to examine Camilla. "Most extraordinary!" He exclaimed. "I've never seen anything like it."

Parent: Are you tired?
Child: (sitting up slightly but still leaning on parent)
Parent: "No," Camilla told him, "I feel fine."

Parent: "Well then," Doctor Bumble said, turning to Miss Cream, "I don't see any reason why she shouldn't go to school tomorrow. Here's some lemon. That should help clear up those stripes in a few days. If it doesn't, you know where to reach me." And off he went."
Child: (leaning into parent, cuddling)

Parent: The next day was a disaster. Everyone at school laughed at Camilla. They called her Camilla Crayon, and Night of the Living Lollipop. She tried her best to act as if everything were normal. But when the class said the pledge of allegiance, her stripes turned red, white, and blue, and she broke out in stars.
Child: (pointing at the tablet and smiling)

Parent: "The other kids thought this was great. One yelled out, 'Let's see some purple polka dots!' Sure enough, Camilla turned all purple and polka dotty. Someone else shouted 'Checker board!' And a pattern of squares covered her skin. Soon everyone was calling out different shapes and colors and poor Camilla was changing faster than you can change channels on a TV." (maintains focus on the tablet)
Child: (leans back and looks at the parent, engaging eye contact)
Parent: "Ding, ding, ding." (continues to look at the tablet)

Parent: "That night, Miss Harms, the school principal called. 'I'm sorry,' Mrs. Cream said, 'I'm going to have to ask you to keep Camilla home from school. She's just too much of a distraction and I've been getting calls from the other parents. They are afraid those stripes might be contagious.'" (smiling)
Child: (standing next to chair, looking away from the tablet)

Parent: (continues reading) "Camilla was so embarrassed. She couldn't believe that two days ago everyone liked her. Now, nobody wanted to be in the same room with her. Her father tried to make her feel better. 'Is there anything I can get you, sweetheart?' He asked."
Child: (climbs onto parent's lap)
Parent: (continues reading) "'No, thank you,' said Camilla. What she really wanted was a nice plate of lima beans but she had been laughed at for one day."
Child: (still on parent's lap, looking at the tablet)

Parent: (points to the tablet and continues reading) "'Hm, well yes I see that,' Doctor Bumble wondered when Mr. Cream phoned the next day. 'I think I'd be better bringing in the specialist. We'll be right over.'"
Child: (leaning against parent, looking at the tablet)

Parent: (continues reading) "About an hour later, Doctor Bumble arrived with four people in long white coats. He introduced them to the Creams. 'This is Doctor Grout, Doctor Sponge, Doctor Cricket, and Doctor Young.' Then the specialists went to work on Camilla. They squeezed, and jabbed, and tapped, and tested. It was very uncomfortable. 'Well, it's not the mumps,' concluded Doctor Grout. 'Or the measles,' said Doctor Sponge. 'Definitely not the chicken pox,' put in Doctor Cricket. 'Or sunburn,' said Doctor Young."
Child: (leaning closer to the tablet)

Parent: (continues reading) "'Try these,' said the specialists. They each handed her a bottle filled with different-colored pills. 'Take one of each before bed,' said Doctor Grout. Then they filed out the front door, followed by Doctor Bumble."
Child: (looking at the tablet together with the parent)

Parent: "The next night, Camilla took her medicine. It was awful. When she woke up the next morning, she did feel different. But when she got dressed, her clothes didn't feel right. She looked in the mirror and there, staring back at her, was a giant multicolored pill with her face on it."
Child: (still looking at the tablet, appears to be focused)
Parent: "Doctor Bumble rushed over as soon as Mrs. Cream called. This time, instead of the specialists, he brought the experts."
Child: (raises and looks at their hand, possibly curious about the story)

Parent: "Doctor Gourd and Mr. Melon were the finest scientific minds in the land. Once again, Camilla was poked and prodded, looked at and listened to. The experts wrote down lots of numbers, then they huddled together and whispered. Doctor Gourd finally spoke, 'It might be a virus,' he announced with authority. Suddenly, fuzzy little virus balls appeared all over Camilla."
Child: (hands down, continues looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Or possibly some form of bacteria," said Mr. Melon. Out popped squiggly, little bacteria tails."
Child: (slightly leaning away from the tablet, looking at the parent)
Parent: "I..."
Child: (looks back at the tablet)
Child: (turns to look at the parent)
Parent: "What?"
Child: (gestures with open hands, looking at the parent)
Parent: "I think they're calling out things that they already know of."
Child: (raises arms, looking excited)
Parent: "And they're just trying to guess what is causing it, so every time they say something, it pops out."
Child: (covers face with hands, looking at the tablet)

Parent: ""Or it could be a fungus," added Doctor Gourd. Instantly, Camilla was covered with different-colored fungus blotches. The experts looked at Camilla, then looked at each other. "We need to go over these numbers and back again at the lab," Doctor Gourd explained. "We'll call you when we know something." But the experts didn't have a clue, much less a cure."
Child: (leans forward, looking at the tablet)

Parent: "By now, the TV news had found out about Camilla. Reporters from every channel were outside her house, telling the story of a bizarre case of the incredible changing kid. Soon, a huge crowd was camped out on the front lawn."
Child: (looking at the tablet, slightly leaning towards the parent)
Parent: "That means the front yard." [Frame 22455]
Child: "Yes." [Frame 22455]

Parent: "The Creams were swamped with all kinds of remedies, from psychologists, or allergists, herbalists, nutritionists, psychics, and old medicine men, a guru, and even a veterinarian." [Frame 22455]
Child: (looking at the tablet quietly)

Parent: "Each so-called cure only added to poor Camilla's strange appearance until it was hard to even recognize her. She sprouted roots, and berries, and crystals, and feathers, and a long furry tail. But nothing worked." [Frame 22455]

Parent: (pointing at the tablet) "One day, a woman who called herself an environmental therapist claimed she could cure Camilla. 'Close your eyes,' she said. 'Breathe deeply, and become one with your room.'"
Child: (still focused on the tablet, appears interested)

Parent: (continuing to point at the tablet) "'I wish you hadn't said that,' Camilla groaned. Slowly, she started to melt into the walls of her room. Her bed became her mouth, her nose was her dresser, and two paintings were her eyes. The therapist screamed and ran from the house."
Child: (maintaining focus on the tablet)

Parent: "'What are we going to do?' Cried Mrs. Cream. 'It just keeps getting worse and worse!' She began to sob. At that moment, Mr. Cream heard a quiet little knock at the front door. He opened it and there stood an old woman who was just as plump and sweet as a strawberry."
Child: (leans back slightly, looking at the parent)
Parent: "Yum. I love strawberries."
Child: (smiling and looking at parent) "Me too."
The scene describes a parent and child reading a storybook together, with the child closely following the narrative and responding positively to the mentions of strawberries toward the end.
Child: (sitting on the parent's lap, looking up)
Parent: “Excuse me,” she said, brightly. “But I think I can help.” She went into Camilla’s room and looked around. “My goodness,” she said, with the shake of her head. “What we have here...”

She ate all the lima beans she wanted and she never had even a touch of stripes again.
